question: According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, the Commanding Officer of the cavalry in the Mauryan administration was known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashwadhyaksha.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Kautilya's Arthashastra,** the **commanding** **officer of the cavalry **in the Mauryan administration was known as **Ashwadhyaksha.**
 
• The term 'Ashwa' means** horse** and 'dhyaksha' means **commander or supervisor.**
 
• The Ashwadhyaksha was responsible for **managing and training **the cavalry soldiers, selecting and breeding horses, and ensuring the proper maintenance of the horses and equipment.
 
• The cavalry played a crucial role in the **Mauryan army, **and the Ashwadhyaksha held an important position in the administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the Mauryan administration, the war office was made up of** six boards.**
 
• **Rathadhyaksha** refers to the commander of the** chariots. **
 
 
• He was also in charge of **paying the workers** who were building chariots.​
 
 
 
• **Hastyadhyaksha **refers to the commander of the **elephants. **
 
• **Patyadhyaksha** refers to the commander of the **infantry.**
